citations.quote: Trial 1 was a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 21-week study (one week post screening, two-week, single-blind placebo run-in, 14-week double-blind treatment, and 4-week no treatment follow-up) in 301 patients with multiple sclerosis at 33 centers in the U.S. and Canada: 229 patients assigned to AMPYRA 10 mg twice daily and 72 patients assigned to placebo.

population.text: Patients with multiple sclerosis able to walk 25 feet in 8-45 seconds; excluded history of seizures or epileptiform EEG activity

citations.quote: Patient inclusion criteria included the ability to walk 25 feet in 8–45 seconds. Patient exclusion criteria included a history of seizures or evidence of epileptiform activity on a screening EEG, and onset of an MS exacerbation within 60 days.

endpoint.text: Timed-Walk Response (consistent improvement in walking speed on the Timed 25-Foot Walk, responder analysis)

citations.quote: The primary measure of efficacy in both trials was walking speed (in feet per second) as measured by the Timed 25-foot Walk (T25W), using a responder analysis.

Trial 1 was a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 21-week study (one week post screening, two-week, single-blind placebo run-in, 14-week double-blind treatment, and 4-week no treatment follow-up) in 301 patients with multiple sclerosis at 33 centers in the U.S. and Canada: 229 patients assigned to AMPYRA 10 mg twice daily and 72 patients assigned to placebo.

In Study F203, 301 subjects were randomized and 283 completed the study. A significantly greater proportion of patients taking Fampridine-SR had a consistent improvement in walking speed, the study's primary outcome, compared to patients taking placebo (34.8% vs. 8.3%) as measured by the Timed 25-Foot Walk (p < 0.001).

Trial 2 was a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 14-week study (one week post-screening, two weeks of single-blind, placebo run-in, nine weeks of double-blind treatment, and two weeks of no-treatment follow-up) in 239 patients with multiple sclerosis at 39 centers in the U.S. and Canada: 120 patients assigned to 10 mg twice daily and 119 assigned to placebo.

In MS-F204, a total of 239 patients with MS were randomized and 227 completed this study. The primary efficacy endpoint for this study was met: the percentage of patients who met the Timed-Walk Responder criterion was 42.9% in the Fampridine-SR-treated group compared with 9.3% in the placebo-treated group (p<0.001).

indication.text: AMPYRA (dalfampridine) is indicated to improve walking in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), demonstrated by an increase in walking speed

citations.quote: AMPYRA (dalfampridine) is indicated as a treatment to improve walking in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). This was demonstrated by an increase in walking speed [see *Clinical Studies* (14)].

target_moa.text: Broad spectrum potassium channel blocker that increases conduction of action potentials in demyelinated axons through inhibition of potassium channels

citations.quote: The mechanism by which dalfampridine exerts its therapeutic effect has not been fully elucidated. Dalfampridine is a broad spectrum potassium channel blocker. In animal studies, dalfampridine has been shown to increase conduction of action potentials in demyelinated axons through inhibition of potassium channels.
